verdict: A beast of a different breed — half game module, half card deck. 'Deck A: Tragic Flaws' and 'Deck B: Barnyard Beatdown' give you Shakespeare's depressives and Shakespeare's clowns colliding across barnyard territory. The Kayfabe philosophy is sharp: 'To Thine Own Self Be True (Or Just Lie Better)' is possibly the best tagline in the corpus. Three gameplay modes (Doom Spiral, Confusion Engine, Mixed Media Mayhem) are mechanically tight but they eat seven of your fifteen pages. Card count is low for a standalone product. Table-ready: Y with a co-facilitator who knows the rules.
blurb: Shakespeare meets barnyard wrestling in a hybrid rules-and-character card module. For drama teachers, improv troupes, and anyone who wants to play Hamlet flipping coins and losing.

coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Title matches content exactly: serious Shakespeare, animal comedy, Kayfabe philosophy.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Shakespeare parody is a well-trodden lane but this spin is genuinely sharp.

coverQA.coverNote: FrizzleBob verdict: strongest cover tagline in the Shakespeare subset, possibly in the whole corpus. 'Or Just Lie Better' is a three-word pitch for Kayfabe. Whoever wrote that line should get a Folio.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: SHAKESPEAREAN ANIMAL BEATDOWN – Shakespeare's Depressives vs His Clowns (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Shakespeare only ever ran two animals: the one too sad to move, and the one too quick to care.

Here is the split your syllabus quietly sanded off. Half the cast broods itself to a standstill, the Depressives, with Hamlet out front flipping a coin he loses no matter which side lands. The other half cannot stay quiet long enough to feel a thing, the Clowns, who turn a funeral into a bit and a bit into an exit. Annotate that and it flatlines on the page. Perform it out loud and you find out, fast, which animal you become the moment a scene starts to slip.

This is the Shakespeare expansion for the Kayfabizarro table: a hybrid rules-and-character module that drops the Bard's two registers straight into Social Story Wrestling. You pull on the mask, perform the line in character, and the room rules whether the scene held or fell apart in your hands.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Animal Beatdown Cards: 7 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" character cards dealt across Meet the Depressives and Meet the Clowns, featuring Ganymede (a disguise wearing a disguise: flirt with a rival while pretending to coach them on how to flirt with you), Hamlet (flip a coin over whether to act, lose either way, and narrate your own paralysis until the table begs you to do anything), and The Changeling Boy (the prize the entire fight is about, who never gets a single line and wins regardless).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook, bolted on as a module. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and one merciless call: a scene the table does not believe never happened.
- The Depressives-versus-Clowns Engine: the working heart of the expansion, where melancholy and mischief stop being themes and become two ways to take a turn, brood for momentum or bolt for cover, with solo and crafting modes for building new fighters into the ring.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
Every classroom that trains you to revere Shakespeare is training you to sit politely through the best fight in the building. I make these so drama teachers, improv troupes, and anyone with a kitchen table can put the play back on its feet and let it misbehave. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, run the match at the next rehearsal. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next deck and the next doomed cast. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The tragedy and the joke were always the same animal in two different hats."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
